solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Object e's taken from back of grave

indicators.note: taken from the back of means the letter is removed from the tail of the word for grave

parts.note: grave means serious and sober, i.e. demure
the letter e named in the clue, here written Cockney-style

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a letter has been chipped off the back of a gravestone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from back of' removes the final E of DEMURE. 'Grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective, and 'Object' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Perhaps Black Beauty has hidden talents

definitions.text: Perhaps Black Beauty has hidden talents

parts.words: Perhaps Black Beauty has hidden talents
parts.note: Black Beauty is a famous black horse in the novel, so literally a black-coated horse; a person with unsuspected abilities is called this too

explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is Anna Sewell's horse; the phrase for an unknown quantity is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone with unsuspected ability, and literally a horse of black colour.

clue.text: Greet the dawn in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: morn is poetic for the morning or dawn

explanation.surface: Saying hello to the sunrise out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is Scots for weep, not say hello.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to greet is to weep or lament.

clue.text: Compensation that's uniform?

definitions.meaning: amends or reparation for a wrong
..., dressed alike again and again, so the same clothing throughout

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as RE-DRESS: clothing repeated, uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress means reparation; split, it suggests dressing identically again.

clue.text: International strike?

definitions.meaning: an international cricket fixture between countries
striking a match tries it out, so a strike is a cryptic trial of a match

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: to test a match is to strike it.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international cricket game, and a whimsical trial of a matchstick is striking it.

clue.text: To walk, climbing boot may have this

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: A hiking boot needs something to walk in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns PACE upwards to ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced front of a boot.

clue.text: Do-or-die struggle below the South entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue below places the jumble under the S

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

indicators.note: struggle suggests writhing about, so the letters move

explanation.surface: A desperate fight beneath the southern entry point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' rearranges DOORDIE to IDEDOOR, placed 'below' S.
explanation.definitionFit: A side door is an entrance at the side of a building.

clue.text: Wind and fog — what Australians take to heart

parts.note: fog is thick mist

indicators.note: the heart of the word Australians is its central run of letters

explanation.surface: Weather report from Down Under about wind and fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take to heart' picks RAL, the middle three letters of AustRALians.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold north wind in southern France.

clue.text: Coast road

parts.note: a strand is a shore, and a famous London street takes its name from the old Thames riverbank

explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a London street originally running along the Thames shore.

clue.text: Little house with a tenant rising to a larger establishment

parts.note: ho is short for house

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: a let is a lease to a tenant

explanation.surface: A cottage with a lodger grows into something grander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LET up to TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a large building for paying guests.

clue.text: Puritan saints shown in a good light here

definitions.meaning: a Parliamentarian of the English Civil War, nicknamed for cropped hair

definitions.text: saints shown in a good light here
definitions.meaning: saints are painted with a halo, a circle of light around the head

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer literally: a head circled by a halo.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were Puritan supporters of Parliament, and a saint's haloed head is literally ringed.

clue.text: Cover girl goes to fantasy movie …

parts.note: a girl is referred to as she
E.T. is Spielberg's fantasy film about an alien

explanation.surface: A cover girl lands a part in a fantasy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover girl' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Cover' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a bed covering.

clue.text: … having unfortunately seen all the grand opera

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Continuing from the fantasy movie, someone sadly saw the whole grand opera too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles SEEN ALL THE GRAND into the fairy-tale opera by Humperdinck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel and Gretel is Humperdinck's operatic version of the fairy tale.

clue.text: Showing negligence with regard to a young lady

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone is being careless in their dealings with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss describes someone careless in their duty.

clue.text: Coat acts on him in a peculiar way

indicators.note: in a peculiar way means oddly arranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A coat has a strange effect on a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a peculiar way' rearranges ACTS ON HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a waterproof raincoat.

clue.text: Check those available to go round and visit

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over
to call on someone is to visit

explanation.surface: Instructions to see who is free to make a round of visits.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll call checks attendance by reading out names.

clue.text: Misguided Spartan queen's tragic dog

parts.note: Leda was Queen of Sparta, mother of Helen
Old Dog Tray is a sad Stephen Foster song about a dog

explanation.surface: A Spartan queen's dog meets a tragic end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be led astray is to be misled.

clue.text: Hazard surrounding a paper's measure

indicators.note: surrounding puts the risk word around the single letter

parts.note: to hazard is to put at risk, imperil

explanation.surface: A risk around a newspaper's chosen standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' is the verb, IMPERIL; 'surrounding' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial is a traditional paper size, 22 by 30 inches.

clue.text: An apology for a dance

definitions.meaning: a ballroom dance where one may cut in on a partner

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase begs pardon, and also names a dance in which partners can be claimed by cutting in.

clue.text: Stores up love in heart that's inclined…

indicators.note: in heart puts the zero in the middle of the turned word
in a down clue up means read upwards

parts.note: depots are storehouses
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Stockpiling love in one's heart leaves one bowed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DEPOTS to STOPED; O goes 'in heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooped means bent forward, leaning.

clue.text: Open letters for detectives

definitions.meaning: the detectives' initials are C, I and D

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads CID, Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, as 'C and ID'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and outspoken; the second reading spells out C and ID.

clue.text: … to welcome a Conservative title

parts.note: a title is a right or claim to something

explanation.surface: Continuing from 19, opening up to greet a Tory's honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to hail or greet with praise.

clue.text: Add a very quiet coda

parts.note: pp is the musical marking pianissimo
a coda is a closing passage, an end

explanation.surface: A musician tacks on a soft closing passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach at the end.

clue.text: Do some nest-feathering — keep cool in nests that are renovated

indicators.note: renovated means done up and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm while birds' nests are being refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges KEEP COOL IN NESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To feather one's nest is to enrich oneself, the same idiom as filling one's pockets.

clue.text: Battle in which we got besieged by the French

indicators.note: besieged by puts the pronoun inside the French article

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Recalling a battle in which our side were surrounded by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewes, 1264, a battle of the Barons' War in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Lewes was fought in Sussex in 1264.

clue.text: Church official carries a flower

definitions.meaning: a lay officer in Presbyterian churches
a shrub bearing creamy blossom used in cordial

explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a presbyter and also a flowering shrub of the genus Sambucus.

clue.text: Cheer on doctor before operation

indicators.note: before puts the doctor ahead of the operation

parts.note: Doctor Who, the BBC time traveller
op is short for a surgical operation

explanation.surface: Urging on a surgeon before surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of joy.

clue.text: Scandinavian man put back in 'amper

indicators.note: in places the turned name inside the other word

parts.note: hamper means hinder; with the h dropped Cockney-style, as the apostrophe shows, it is inder

indicators.note: put back means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Alec is a man's name

explanation.surface: A Norseman is stuffed back into a hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns ALEC into CELA, which goes 'in' INDER, h-less 'inder' for hinder (hamper). The apostrophe on 'amper signals the dropped H.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a native of Iceland, a Nordic country.

clue.text: Fools about outside church at set times

indicators.note: outside puts the turned word around the church letters
about means the word for fools is turned round

parts.note: to fool is to delude, so fools = deludes

explanation.surface: Jesters loiter around a church on a timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DELUDES to SEDULED, which goes 'outside' CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scheduled happens at planned, fixed times.

clue.text: Take a wife, indeed!

definitions.meaning: an archaic exclamation of surprise, 'by Mary'

explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to wed, and the old oath 'marry!' meant truly or forsooth.
